problem.statement: GPU-driver-specific memory leaks in WPF's hardware-accelerated rendering pipeline (e.g. on Nvidia Quadro cards) force developers to choose between disabling hardware acceleration entirely or shipping an app that leaks memory on affected hardware.

persona.primary: WPF developer building graphics/drawing-heavy desktop applications

context.situation: A developer drawing custom patterns in WPF on a high-resolution monitor traced a memory leak to specific Nvidia Quadro GPU drivers, confirming it did not reproduce on GeForce or AMD hardware.

current_workarounds: Setting RenderOptions.ProcessRenderMode to SoftwareOnly to disable hardware acceleration and avoid the leak, at the cost of rendering performance elsewhere in the app
existing_substitutes: SkiaSharp (rendering library in use when the leak was observed, tested across versions 2.88.9 and 3.116.0)

possible_wedges.offer: A standalone WPF render diagnostics tool that runs an app under different GPU/driver profiles and flags known driver-specific leak patterns before release.
A CLI audit check that inspects a WPF app's render mode settings and GPU driver environment, warning when hardware acceleration is likely to trigger known leak signatures on specific driver families.

risks: Only a single evidence item (one GitHub bug report), no corroborating reports of this exact driver/leak combination
Commercial intent and commitment signals in the evidence are very low (0.1 each), suggesting this is a bug report, not a purchase intent signal
Unclear how many WPF shops specifically target Quadro-class workstation GPUs versus consumer hardware, limiting addressable market
No indication the reporter or others would pay for tooling versus wanting a free upstream fix in SkiaSharp/WPF itself

cheapest_experiment.hypothesis: WPF developers hitting GPU-driver-specific rendering leaks would want an automated audit that flags the risk before shipping, rather than manually bisecting drivers like this reporter did.
cheapest_experiment.input: Reply to this and similar SkiaSharp/WPF GitHub issues offering a free one-page 'GPU render leak checklist' plus a link to sign up for early access to an automated audit check.
cheapest_experiment.output: Number of sign-ups or replies expressing interest from developers who hit the same class of driver-specific leak.
cheapest_experiment.commitment_event: Developer provides email or app details to be notified when the audit check is available.
cheapest_experiment.success_threshold: 5+ developers across distinct threads/projects sign up or ask for the tool within 2 weeks
cheapest_experiment.failure_threshold: Fewer than 2 sign-ups after posting in 3+ relevant issue threads, or responses indicating the community expects this to be fixed upstream for free
